---
title: "Previewing"
---

`q2 preview` opens your document or website in a browser and keeps it
up to date as you edit. It has two modes.

| | `q2 preview` (default) | `q2 preview --static` |
|---|---|---|
| What runs | A live session: pages render in the browser as you type | A real `q2 render` to disk, served by a plain static server |
| On save | The page updates in place; open menus, scroll position and math survive | The changed page re-renders; the browser reloads |
| What you see | The page being edited | Exactly what `q2 render` produces, including the sitemap, listings, search index and scripts |
| Code cells | Executed on the server, re-executed on request | Executed only for pages you open (see below) |
| Best for | Writing and editing | Checking the finished site, or a workflow like Quarto 1's `quarto preview` |

## The default preview

``` {.bash filename="Terminal"}
q2 preview                # the project in the current directory
q2 preview posts/one.qmd  # open on a specific page
q2 preview notes.qmd      # a document outside any project
```

The browser opens automatically. Edits appear within a fraction of a
second without rebuilding the page, so JavaScript state is preserved
across edits. See the `--help` text for the flags that control the
port, the browser, and live sharing.

### Typst documents

A page whose format is `typst` or `pdf` shows its PDF in the preview, in
a pdf.js viewer, and recompiles it shortly after you stop typing. A
compile that fails keeps the last good PDF on screen under an error
banner. When you reached the page from another one,
a **Back** button at the left of the viewer's toolbar returns to it. In a
book project the preview shows the page you are on, not the whole book.

A page that sets `output-ext` to something other than `pdf` (typst source,
say) has no PDF to show, so it keeps the "no live preview" notice.

The compile runs the `typst` on your `PATH`, and writes into
`.quarto/preview-out/` under the project (git-ignored, swept at startup),
so the project directory must be writable. This view has no **Download
as** menu; that is part of the editor UI below.

### Render options in the live viewer

`q2 preview --to FORMAT`, `-M KEY:VALUE` and `--profile NAME` work as
for `q2 render` ([Render options](render-options.qmd)); for instance
`q2 preview book/ --to typst` shows PDF panes. Notes:

- They are refused with `--ui editor` (the editor has its own settings),
  `--join` and `--no-project`.
- `--to` and `-M` are applied to the page preview, the PDF pane and the
  downloads. They do not reach code execution.
- `-M book-scope:...` is ignored (a startup notice says so): the viewer
  renders one page at a time, and the PDF pane always asks for the
  chapter.
- `--profile` works as `QUARTO_PROFILE` does: the PDF pane, downloads and
  the server's project settings honor it, but the page you edit is
  rendered in the browser from the synced project, which has no profile
  files, so the html preview ignores it (a startup notice says so).
- `--to typst` with a page that sets `output-ext: typ` passes the check
  but has no live preview.
- With `--share`, the `-M` values and `--to` are sent to every guest's
  browser. Do not put secrets in `-M`.

## The editor UI

``` {.bash filename="Terminal"}
q2 preview --ui editor    # the quarto-hub editor, served by q2
```

`--ui editor` serves the same editor as quarto-hub: a source editor
next to the preview, with a **Download as** menu and an **Import**
button. Everything the browser version of quarto-hub does in the
browser, the editor UI asks `q2` to do with the pandoc and typst on
your machine:

- **Download as** produces Word (`.docx`), OpenDocument (`.odt`),
  PowerPoint (`.pptx`), EPUB, Typst source (`.typ`) and PDF. The file
  is rendered from what is in the editor, saved or not. Code-cell
  output is included, Word comments and tracked changes carry the
  author's name, and a notice says how many code cells were not
  executed.
- **Typst documents** (`format: typst` or `format: pdf`) show the PDF
  in the preview pane and re-render it as you type. A render that
  fails keeps the last good PDF on screen under an error banner.
- **Books.** On a chapter of a book project, the Typst source, PDF and
  EPUB entries come in pairs: **Download book as** renders the whole
  book into one file named for the book (`My-Book.pdf`), and **This
  chapter only** renders just the page you are on. (Word, OpenDocument
  and PowerPoint have no whole-book output, so they always download the
  page.) A page that is not listed in the book's `chapters` downloads on
  its own, with a notice (`Q-5-41`) saying why it is not the book.
- **Import** reads docx, odt, rtf, epub and pptx files into a new
  document, with its images stored next to it in `<name>_media/`. The
  result is created in the editing session; it reaches your files on
  disk only when you started `q2 preview` with `--allow-edit`, as for
  any other edit. Images larger than 10 MB are not stored, as in
  quarto-hub.

These need `pandoc` on your `PATH`, and `typst` for Typst and PDF
output. When one is missing, the preview pane or the download says so
(`Q-20-1`, `Q-20-2`, `Q-21-1`) rather than offering nothing. Typst
packages that `q2` does not carry (`@preview/...`, including the book
template's) are fetched from the Typst package registry, so a first PDF
of a document that uses one needs network access.

The PDF you get here and the PDF quarto-hub makes in the browser are
both correct but not byte-for-byte identical. quarto-hub compiles with
a pinned Typst and a bundled font set; `q2 preview` uses the `typst`
installed on your machine, your system fonts and real Typst packages.
Line breaks and font fallbacks can differ between the two.

The typst source download is the bare `.typ` file; images are not
bundled with it.

### What a book download does and does not include

- Only the page open in the editor is rendered from its editor text.
  Every other chapter is read from disk, so unsaved edits to those are
  not in the download (and, without `--allow-edit`, edits made in the
  editor are never on disk).
- Pre-render and post-render scripts do not run, and the book's own
  `output-ext` is ignored: **Typst source** is a `.typ` and **PDF** is a
  `.pdf`, whatever the project says.
- Code cells are not executed for a download. Output that was recorded
  while you edited is included; a notice counts the cells that had none.
  A chapter that `embed`s a cell from another chapter needs that cell's
  executed output, so downloading *that book* whole can fail; the
  chapter alone still downloads.
- The project's own `_book/` directory and render manifests are not
  touched.
- One book download per project runs at a time. A second request while
  one is running is answered "the preview server is busy"; try again when
  the first finishes. A small book takes a second or two; a large one
  can take much longer, and cancelling takes effect between chapters.

### Sharing

With `--share`, anyone holding the join string can ask the host to run
renders, downloads and imports: those requests use the host's `pandoc`
and `typst` and read the host's project, and an import uploads the file
to the host (up to 25 MB), where it is converted by a sandboxed `pandoc`.
Treat the join string like a password, as the `--share` help says.

## Static preview

``` {.bash filename="Terminal"}
q2 preview --static                # render the project, serve it, watch for changes
q2 preview --static posts/one.qmd  # the whole project, opened on that page
q2 preview --static notes.qmd      # a lone document
```

`--static` first renders everything to disk, exactly as `q2 render`
does, then serves the output directory (`_site` for a website) on a
local port and opens the browser. It then watches your files:

- Saving a page re-renders that page (and any page that depends on it,
  such as a listing that includes it) and reloads the browser, opening
  the page you changed.
- Saving `_quarto.yml`, a `_metadata.yml`, a stylesheet, an image, an
  extension file, or anything else that is not a page re-renders the
  whole project and reloads the browser in place.
- A save that fails to render leaves the previous output in place and
  shows the error in a panel at the bottom of the page. Fix the file and
  the page reloads.

Each re-render is a real render: pre-render and post-render scripts
run, and the output directory is what you would publish.

### Typst and PDF

`--static` also serves `format: typst` output. The rendered `.pdf` opens
in a pdf.js viewer rather than the browser's own PDF viewer, and the
viewer reloads when a re-render finishes, keeping your page and zoom.
For a book project, `--static` renders and serves the whole book, and a
saved chapter rebuilds the whole book. The viewer needs `typst` on your
`PATH`, like the render itself. `--static` does not serve other non-HTML
formats (`docx`, `pptx`, `epub`): they are refused once, before anything
renders. A render that writes nothing shows its diagnostics in the
browser instead of an empty page.

### Flags

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--no-watch` | Render once and serve; never re-render |
| `--no-navigate` | After a re-render, reload the current page instead of opening the page that changed |
| `--to FORMAT` | The output format, as `q2 render --to`. Only `html`, `revealjs` and `typst` can be served |
| `-M KEY:VALUE` | Metadata for the whole session, as `q2 render -M` |
| `--profile NAME` | The active profile(s), as `q2 render --profile` |
| `--port N`, `--host H` | Where to listen. Default: a free port on `127.0.0.1` |
| `--no-browser`, `--browser APP` | Do not open a browser, or open a specific one |

`--to`, `-M` and `--profile` mean here what they mean for `q2 render`
([Render options](render-options.qmd)). `-M book-scope:chapter` on a book
exits with [`Q-5-47`](../../errors/project/Q-5-47.qmd), because the flag is
fixed for the session and a whole book can never be one chapter.

The live-session flags (`--share`, `--allow-edit`, `--ui`, `--join`)
do not apply to static mode.

### Code execution

A static preview does not execute every page's code up front: a site
with many Jupyter or knitr pages would take a long time to start. Pages
whose code has not run are served with their code cells shown as
source, and the first time you open such a page it is executed and
reloaded. Pages you have opened stay executed through later re-renders.

To never execute code in a preview, set this in `_quarto.yml`:

``` {.yaml filename="_quarto.yml"}
preview:
  engine: off
```

This is the same key the default preview uses.

### Defaults in `_quarto.yml`

Quarto 1's `project: preview:` keys set the defaults for static mode;
command-line flags override them.

``` {.yaml filename="_quarto.yml"}
project:
  type: website
  preview:
    port: 4321
    host: 127.0.0.1
    browser: false
    watch-inputs: false
    navigate: false
```

The `timeout` and `serve` keys from Quarto 1 are not supported. They are
reported once at startup and otherwise ignored.
